chapters.title: No Other Gospel
chapters.html:
Galatians 1

Greeting

1Paul, an apostle — not from men nor through a man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead —

2and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:

3Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,

4who gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,

5to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.

No Other Gospel

6I am astonished that you are so quickly turning away from Him who called you in the grace of Christ, to a different gospel —

7not that there is another one, but there are some who are troubling you and want to distort the gospel of Christ.

8But even if we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you a gospel other than the one we preached to you, let him be accursed.

9As we have said before, so now I say again: if anyone preaches to you a gospel other than the one you received, let him be accursed.

10Am I now trying to win over men, or God? Or am I seeking to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I would not be a servant of Christ.

Called by God

11For I want you to know, brothers, that the gospel preached by me is not of human origin.

12I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it; it came through a revelation of Jesus Christ.

13For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how I persecuted the church of God beyond measure and tried to destroy it,

14and I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my own age among my people, being far more zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

15But when He who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me by His grace was pleased

16to reveal His Son in me, so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not at once consult with flesh and blood,

17nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia, and returned again to Damascus.

18Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to get to know Cephas, and stayed with him fifteen days.

19I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord's brother.

20In what I am writing to you, I tell you before God, I am not lying.

21Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

22I was still unknown in person to the churches of Judea that are in Christ;

23they were only hearing it said, "The man who once persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy."

24They glorified God because of me.

Notes

  • vv8–9 "let him be accursed" — anathema, the Greek Bible's word for what is under the ban, given up wholly to God: Jericho, The city and all that is in it will be devoted to the LORD (Joshua 6:17), anathema in the Greek. Paul lays it on any other gospel, even one from himself or an angel from heaven, and says it twice.

  • vv15–16 "He who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me… so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles" — the call of the prophets. The LORD called me from the womb; from my mother's body He named my name, ek koilias mētros mou ekalese in the Greek, Paul's words, is the servant whom the LORD gives as a light for the nations (Isaiah 49:1, 6). Jeremiah too was set apart before you came out of the womb… a prophet to the nations (Jeremiah 1:5). Ethnē, nations, is the word Paul uses for the Gentiles.

chapters.title: Justified by Faith
chapters.html:
Galatians 2

Accepted by the Apostles

1Then after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along also.

2I went up because of a revelation, and I set before them the gospel I preach among the Gentiles, privately, before those who were held in high regard, to make sure I was not running, and had not run, in vain.

3But not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, though he was a Greek.

4The question arose because of false brothers secretly brought in, who slipped in to spy out the freedom we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might enslave us.

5We did not yield to them in submission even for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.

6As for those who were held in high regard — whatever they once were makes no difference to me; God shows no partiality — those men added nothing to me.

7On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted with the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been with the gospel to the circumcised,

8for He who worked through Peter for his apostleship to the circumcised worked also through me for the Gentiles;

9and when James and Cephas and John, who were held to be pillars, recognized the grace that had been given to me, they gave Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship, so that we would go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised.

10They asked only that we remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do.

Paul Opposes Cephas

11But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.

12Before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; but when they came, he drew back and kept himself apart, fearing those of the circumcision.

13The rest of the Jews joined him in playing the hypocrite, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.

14But when I saw that they were not walking straight by the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, "If you, a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?"

Justified by Faith

15We ourselves are Jews by birth and not sinners from among the Gentiles,

16yet we know that a person is not justified by works of the Law but through faith in Jesus Christ. So we also have believed in Christ Jesus, in order to be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the Law, because by works of the Law no flesh will be justified.

17But if, in seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, is Christ then a minister of sin? By no means!

18For if I build up again what I tore down, I show myself to be a transgressor.

19For through the Law I died to the Law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ.

20It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. The life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me.

21I do not set aside the grace of God, for if righteousness comes through the Law, then Christ died for nothing.

Notes

  • v16 "through faith in Jesus Christ… we also have believed in Christ Jesus… by faith in Christ" — dia pisteōs Iēsou Christou and ek pisteōs Christou, word for word through the faith of Jesus Christ and by the faith of Christ: faith in Christ, or Christ's own faithfulness. Paul says the phrase twice and puts we have believed in Christ Jesus between them; it comes back in v20 and 3:22. The last line, by works of the Law no flesh will be justified, is Psalm 143:2 in the Greek, no one living will be justified before You; the Hebrew has no one living is righteous before You.

chapters.title: The Promise to Abraham
chapters.html:
Galatians 3

By Faith, Not by Works of the Law

1Foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified.

2Let me ask you only this: did you receive the Spirit by works of the Law, or by hearing with faith?

3Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now finishing by the flesh?

4Did you suffer so much for nothing — if it really was for nothing?

5Does He who supplies the Spirit to you and works mighty works among you do it by works of the Law, or by hearing with faith?

6Just as Abraham "believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness,"

7know then that it is those of faith who are the sons of Abraham.

8The Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham: "In you all the nations shall be blessed."

9So those who are of faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.

The Curse of the Law

10For all who depend on works of the Law are under a curse, for it is written: "Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all the things written in the book of the Law, to do them."

11It is plain that no one is justified before God by the Law, for "The righteous will live by faith."

12But the Law is not of faith; rather, "The person who does them shall live by them."

13Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law by becoming a curse for us, for it is written: "Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree,"

14so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

The Law and the Promise

15Brothers, let me give an example from everyday life: even a man's covenant, once it has been ratified, no one sets aside or adds to.

16The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say "and to seeds," as of many, but as of one, "and to your seed," who is Christ.

17This is what I mean: the Law, which came four hundred and thirty years afterward, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to make the promise void.

18For if the inheritance comes from the Law, it no longer comes from the promise; but God gave it freely to Abraham through a promise.

19Why then the Law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise had been made, and it was ordained by angels through a mediator.

20Now a mediator does not stand for one party only, but God is one.

21Is the Law then against the promises of God? By no means! For if a law had been given that could give life, then righteousness would indeed be by the Law.

22But the Scripture has shut up everything under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.

23Before faith came, we were held in custody under the Law, shut up until the faith that was to come would be revealed.

24So the Law was our guardian until Christ came, so that we might be justified by faith.

25But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.

One in Christ

26For in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith.

27As many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

28There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is no male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.

29If you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's seed, heirs according to the promise.

Notes

  • v10 "Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all the things written in the book of the Law" — Deuteronomy 27:26 as the Greek has it, Cursed is every man who does not continue in all the words of this law. The Hebrew has neither every nor all: Cursed is he who does not uphold the words of this instruction by doing them. Paul's argument stands on the Greek's all, and he says it again: whoever is circumcised is bound to keep the whole Law (5:3).

  • v13 "becoming a curse for us… Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree" — Deuteronomy 21:23, of an executed man's body left on a tree: one who is hanged is a curse of God, in the Greek cursed by God is everyone who is hanged on a tree. Paul quotes it without by God, and with the word Cursed, epikataratos, of the verse he has just quoted (v10), so that both sayings open alike.

  • vv15, 17 "a man's covenant… a covenant previously ratified by God" — diathēkē, the Greek Bible's word for God's covenant, is also a man's will, his last testament, as in Hebrews 9:16, where there is a will, the death of the one who made it must be established. Paul's example works in both senses: a will, once sealed, no one may change (v15); God's covenant with Abraham, sealed before the Law, the Law does not change (v17).

  • v16 "and to your seed," who is Christ — the promise to you and to your seed (Genesis 13:15; 17:8; 24:7). Zera in Hebrew and sperma in Greek are singular and usually mean a whole line of descendants. Paul reads the singular as one person, Christ, and in v29 widens it again to all who belong to Him: you are Abraham's seed.

  • vv19–20 "ordained by angels through a mediator… God is one" — the angels are in the Greek of Moses' blessing, at His right hand angels with Him, where the Hebrew has a fiery law for them (Deuteronomy 33:2); Stephen says the same (Acts 7:53). The mediator is Moses: the laws the LORD gave on Mount Sinai, through Moses (Leviticus 26:46), en cheiri Mōysē, Paul's phrase. God is one is the Shema, the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4). A mediator stands between two parties; the promise God gave Abraham by Himself (v18).

  • vv24–25 "our guardian until Christ came" — paidagōgos, child-leader, the guardian Paul set against a father in 1 Corinthians 4:15, like the trustees and managers who have charge of the heir until the date set by his father (4:2). Eis Christon can mean until Christ or to lead us to Christ. The verses around it measure time: before faith came… until the faith that was to come… now that faith has come.

  • v28 "there is no male and female" — ouk eni arsen kai thēly. The first two pairs are joined by nor; the third by and, in the words of creation, male and female He created them (Genesis 1:27), arsen kai thēly in the Greek. What God made two at the beginning are, with Jew and Greek, slave and free, all one in Christ Jesus.

chapters.title: Sons, Not Slaves
chapters.html:
Galatians 4

Sons and Heirs

1What I am saying is this: as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, though he is the owner of everything,

2but he is under trustees and managers until the date set by his father.

3So with us: when we were children, we were enslaved under the elements of the world.

4But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under the Law,

5to redeem those who were under the Law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.

6Because you are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying, "Abba! Father!"

7So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and if a son, then an heir through God.

8Formerly, when you did not know God, you were slaves to those that by nature are not gods.

9But now that you have come to know God — or rather to be known by God — how can you turn back again to the weak and poor elements, and want to be slaves to them all over again?

10You observe days and months and seasons and years!

11I am afraid for you, that I may have labored over you in vain.

Paul's Appeal

12Become as I am, for I also have become as you are, brothers, I beg you. You did me no wrong.

13You know that it was because of a weakness of the flesh that I first preached the gospel to you,

14and though my condition was a trial to you, you did not despise or spurn me, but received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.

15Where then is the blessing you felt? For I testify to you that, if it had been possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.

16Have I then become your enemy by telling you the truth?

17They court you eagerly, but not for good; they want to shut you out, so that you will court them.

18It is good to be courted for a good purpose always, and not only when I am present with you,

19my children, for whom I am again in the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you!

20I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, for I am perplexed about you.

Hagar and Sarah

21Tell me, you who want to be under the Law, do you not listen to the Law?

22For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and one by the free woman.

23But the son of the slave woman was born according to the flesh, and the son of the free woman through the promise.

24These things are said as an allegory: these women are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children for slavery; she is Hagar.

25Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia; she corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery with her children.

26But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.

27For it is written:
"Rejoice, barren one, who did not bear;
break out and shout, you who were not in labor!
For the children of the desolate one are more
than the children of the one who has a husband."

28Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of the promise.

29But just as at that time the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit, so it is now also.

30But what does the Scripture say? "Drive out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman."

31So, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.

Notes

  • vv3, 9 "the elements of the world… the weak and poor elements" — stoicheia, things set in a row. The word is used of the first lessons, the first principles of God's words (Hebrews 5:12), and of what the world is made of, the working of the elements (Wisdom of Solomon 7:17; 2 Peter 3:10). Here they are things one is enslaved under (v3) and slaves to (v9), set beside those that by nature are not gods (v8). So the word can be read as the first lessons of a child under guardians (vv1–2), the elements of the world, or powers served as gods. Elements keeps all three, as the Greek does.

  • vv24–27 "these women are two covenants… the Jerusalem above… Rejoice, barren one" — Isaiah 54:1 is spoken to the barren, desolate one the LORD calls back as a wife, For your Maker is your husband (54:5–6). Isaiah has already joined Zion to Sarah, Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you… For the LORD comforts Zion (51:2–3), and in the Greek one verb runs through both, ōdinō, to be in labor: Sarah who was in labor with you (51:2), the barren one who was not in labor (54:1). Paul uses it of himself in v19, I am again in the pains of childbirth.

  • vv29–30 "persecuted… Drive out the slave woman" — Genesis says that Sarah saw Hagar's son laughing (21:9), metsacheq, from the root of Isaac's name; the Greek has playing with Isaac her son. The words Paul calls the Scripture are Sarah's (21:10), with the son of the free woman where she said my son, with Isaac, and God told Abraham, All that Sarah says to you — listen to her voice (21:12).
